analyst.summary: SBI's FY26 numbers show a bank in genuinely strong health wearing a deceptively soft top-line growth number. GNPA/NNPA (1.49%/0.39%), SMA (7bps of loans) and provisioning coverage (74-92%) are all at or near multi-decade bests, and CRAR (15.40%, CET-1 12.29%) sits comfortably above the regulatory floor with no capital-raise pressure. The 5.0% one-year revenue growth against a 13.6% three-year CAGR is a real deceleration, not a base effect -- domestic NIM compressed 18bp for the year (21bp in Q4 alone) as the repo-linked loan book repriced down faster than deposit costs, even as loan volumes grew a strong 16.87% YoY; standalone profit still grew 12.88% to a record Rs 80,032 crore, partly aided by a falling credit cost (0.37%) and a lower Q4 tax rate that have limited further room to help. At about 11.9x earnings and 1.6x book against an 18%-plus standalone ROE, the stock looks genuinely cheap rather than cheap-for-a-reason-that-matters, and the imminent SBI Funds Management AMC listing (July 21, 2026, valuing the subsidiary up to Rs 1.17 lakh crore) is a live catalyst for sharper sum-of-the-parts recognition. Hold.
